title: Selvage Session Protocol — the members every frame shares
description: Scalars and small objects of `selvage/2`: the wire version, peer records, document paths, request ids. Valid against PROTOCOL.md §4–§6. Every object here tolerates members it does not know (CANONICAL.md §3), so no schema in this directory forbids one.

version.description: The `v` member of every text frame: the wire version of the frame's sender. The protocol has one wire version, so this is a constant and not a grammar: there is no version to negotiate, and a producer writes exactly this. The byte form is CANONICAL.md §2.5.

requestId.description: A client-assigned request id, unique per connection and never reused for the life of that connection. Bounded at 2^53-1 because a JavaScript receiver cannot hold a larger integer exactly (CANONICAL.md §2.4).

peerId.description: A server-assigned, opaque, room-unique identifier. It does not survive a reconnect: a reconnecting client is a new peer (§9.1). The reference server mints `p-<16 hex>`. It is the server's label for a seat, and the identity a room's contents are keyed by is the key that verified, in the host's sealed state (`PROTOCOL.md` §13.4).

roomId.description: An opaque room identifier. The reference server mints `r-<12 hex>`. A spec may pin a format later; today a client must treat it as opaque (`NOTES.md` §B.12).

token.description: The invite token: the permission to join the room (§9). Carried in the connection URL by a joiner and echoed exactly once, in `room.created`. The reference server mints 32 hex characters. The permission to *read* the room is the key the invite's fragment carries, which the server never sees (§5.1).

not.description: The `Cc` category, negated: C0 (U+0000–U+001F), DELETE (U+007F) and C1 (U+0080–U+009F). A `pattern` is a search and the dialect has no negation of its own, so the exclusion is `not` around one that matches a control character anywhere in the string. Anchoring a single pattern instead would have to agree with every implementation about `$` and a trailing newline, which Python's `re` does not: it matches `$` before one, so a path ending in LF would pass.

documentPath.description: A workspace-relative path: non-empty after trimming, free of control characters (the Unicode `Cc` category), and otherwise unvalidated in this slice (`PROTOCOL.md` §5, `NOTES.md` §B.8). A path is a name and never a promise that a file exists or is readable. It is not read at a method — this version has none that carries one — so a receiver applies the rule where it meets a path, in the host's sealed listing and in a peer's sealed holds: it *drops the path* and applies the rest, refusing neither the frame nor the state (`PROTOCOL.md` §13.3, §13.7). The `not` above is the rule itself, and `common.json` is where `validate.py` drives it.

awarenessClientId.description: A y-protocols awareness client id. Supplied by the client in `session.hello` and echoed on its `PeerInfo`, so an editor adapter can join a cursor to a display name without putting identity into awareness (§8.4).

not.description: The `Cc` category, negated: C0 (U+0000–U+001F), DELETE (U+007F) and C1 (U+0080–U+009F), the same exclusion `documentPath` carries and for the same reason.

displayName.description: At most 32 UTF-16 code units (PROTOCOL.md §5), so an astral character costs two, and free of control characters (the Unicode `Cc` category); `maxLength` counts Unicode code points, so an implementation that enforces the protocol's UTF-16 bound counts UTF-16 code units itself. The server answers `bad_params` for a blank, longer or control-carrying name, and never truncates one.

peer.description: A participant, as the session layer sees one. Identity is the display name and nothing else: the server seats nobody as anything, and the roles a room has are the host's to assign and sign, in the sealed room state (`PROTOCOL.md` §1.2, §7.1).

awareness_client_id.description: Omitted when the connection did not claim one.

documentList.description: A list of document paths, in ascending order by UTF-16 code unit (CANONICAL.md §2.7). It is not carried by a session frame of this version: the room's listing is the `listing` of the host's sealed room state and the paths a peer holds are the set of its sealed holds (`PROTOCOL.md` §7.1, §13.7), and both are canonical under §2.7. That order is the only one this protocol promises for a list of paths.
